chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from al-Bakr ibn Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from his father, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the year, how many days is it? He replied: Three hundred and sixty days. Among them are six days in which God, the Exalted, created the world. That is why they were subtracted from the original year, so the year became three hundred and fifty-four days.
ai.seo_question: How many days are in a lunar year according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* elucidates the lunar calendar's structure, positing a 360-day cycle where the six days of Creation were subtracted to establish the 354-day lunar year. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking cosmological events, such as the six days of creation, directly to the temporal framework of religious observance and ritual timing.
